learn.hook: A single Amoeba becomes two, a Bryophyllum leaf sprouts baby plants — some living things need no partner at all!
points: Reproduction makes copies of DNA, the blueprint of the body. Copying is never perfectly exact, so small variations arise; these help species survive when the environment changes.

Fission: in binary fission one cell splits into two (Amoeba can split in any plane; Leishmania, which causes kala-azar, splits in a definite plane). In multiple fission, as in Plasmodium (malaria parasite), one cell divides into many.
Fragmentation: a filament of Spirogyra breaks into pieces that grow into new individuals. Regeneration: Hydra and Planaria can regrow a whole body from a cut piece using specialised cells.

Budding: a bud grows out of the parent (Hydra, yeast) and later detaches. Spore formation: bread mould (Rhizopus) makes spores in sporangia; spores have thick walls that protect them until they reach moist surfaces.

Vegetative propagation: new plants from roots, stems or leaves — Bryophyllum buds in leaf notches; layering or grafting in sugarcane, roses and grapes. Such plants flower and fruit earlier and are genetically similar to the parent. Banana, orange, rose and jasmine are grown this way because they have lost the capacity to produce seeds.

example.q: Think it through: why do gardeners grow jasmine (mogra) by layering or cuttings instead of from seed?
steps: Jasmine has lost the capacity to produce seeds.
Vegetative propagation produces new plants from stems.
These plants flower earlier and are like the parent.
example.answer: Because jasmine cannot produce seeds, so it is propagated vegetatively — and it flowers sooner.

learn.reallife: When stale bread grows a fuzzy black-grey layer, that is Rhizopus mould sending out countless spores — keep bread dry and covered!

games.title: Which method of asexual reproduction?
items: Amoeba splitting into two
Plasmodium dividing into many cells
Leishmania splitting in a definite plane
Hydra growing a bud on its side
Yeast cell forming a small outgrowth
Rhizopus releasing spores from sporangia
Bryophyllum leaf producing plantlets
New sugarcane from stem pieces

games.title: Asexual reproduction: true or false?
items: DNA copying always produces exactly identical copies.
Copying has small errors, which create variations.
Plasmodium reproduces by multiple fission.
One cell divides into many daughter cells.
Spirogyra reproduces by fragmentation.
Its filament breaks into pieces that grow into new plants.
Plants raised by vegetative propagation take longer to flower than those from seeds.
They usually flower and fruit earlier.
Variations can help a species survive changes in the environment.
Some variants may survive, e.g. a rise in water temperature.
Planaria can regenerate a complete organism from a small piece.
Specialised cells divide and develop into the missing parts.

quiz.q: Why are small variations produced during reproduction?
options: DNA copying is not perfectly accurate
Sunlight changes the DNA every day
quiz.explain: No copying process is perfect; small changes in DNA copies lead to variation.
steps: Reproduction involves making copies of DNA.
No copying process is perfectly accurate.
The small changes in the copies show up as variations.
So variations arise because DNA copying is not perfectly accurate.
Answer: DNA copying is not perfectly accurate

quiz.q: Which organism reproduces by multiple fission?
quiz.explain: Plasmodium, the malaria parasite, divides into many daughter cells at once.
steps: In multiple fission one cell divides into many daughter cells at once.
Plasmodium (the malaria parasite) does this.
Amoeba uses binary fission; Hydra buds; Spirogyra fragments.
So the answer is Plasmodium.
Answer: Plasmodium

quiz.q: Hydra reproduces by —
quiz.explain: Hydra forms buds from regenerative cells, and it can also regenerate from pieces.
steps: Hydra forms buds that grow and detach.
It can also regrow a whole body from a cut piece (regeneration).
So Hydra reproduces by budding and regeneration.
Answer: Budding and regeneration
quiz.mistake: Thinks each organism uses only one method

quiz.q: Bread mould (Rhizopus) reproduces by —
quiz.explain: Sporangia on its hyphae release thick-walled spores that grow on moist surfaces.
steps: Bread mould (Rhizopus) forms sporangia on its threads.
These release thick-walled spores that grow on moist surfaces.
So it reproduces by spore formation.
Answer: Spore formation

quiz.q: Which plant has lost the capacity to produce seeds and is grown by vegetative propagation?
quiz.explain: Banana (like orange, rose and jasmine) is propagated vegetatively because it has lost the ability to produce seeds.
steps: Banana, orange, rose and jasmine have lost the capacity to produce seeds.
So they are grown by vegetative propagation.
Mustard, pea and wheat grow from seeds.
So the answer is banana.
Answer: Banana

quiz.q: Leaves of Bryophyllum can produce new plants because —
options: They have buds in the notches along their margins
quiz.explain: Buds in the leaf notches fall on soil and grow into new plants.
steps: Bryophyllum leaves have buds in the notches along their margins.
These buds fall on soil and grow into new plants.
So its leaves can produce new plants because of these buds.
Answer: They have buds in the notches along their margins

quiz.q: Which is an advantage of vegetative propagation?
options: Plants bear flowers and fruits earlier than those grown from seeds
It can be done only in animals
quiz.explain: Vegetatively propagated plants flower and fruit sooner and keep the parent's features.
steps: Vegetatively propagated plants flower and fruit earlier than plants grown from seed.
They are genetically similar to the parent, so they do not create new varieties.
So the advantage: they bear flowers and fruits earlier.
Answer: Plants bear flowers and fruits earlier than those grown from seeds
quiz.mistake: Thinks it creates lots of variety

quiz.q: Leishmania differs from Amoeba in binary fission because —
options: Leishmania splits in a definite plane related to its whip-like structure
quiz.explain: Amoeba can split in any plane, but Leishmania splits in a definite orientation.
steps: Amoeba can split in any plane during binary fission.
Leishmania splits in a definite plane, related to its whip-like structure.
So Leishmania splits in a definite plane related to its whip-like structure.
Answer: Leishmania splits in a definite plane related to its whip-like structure
quiz.mistake: Assumes all binary fission is the same

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can one Amoeba make babies alone? And why aren't all babies exact copies?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Amoeba splits by fission after copying its DNA — and tiny copying errors create variation!
teach.nudge: Good! But why are the copies not perfectly identical?

revise.summary: Reproduction copies DNA, and small copying errors give variation that helps species survive. Single organisms reproduce asexually by fission, fragmentation, regeneration, budding, spores and vegetative propagation.
focus: Explain why DNA copying produces variation
Match organisms to their method: Amoeba, Leishmania, Plasmodium, Spirogyra, Hydra, Planaria, yeast, Rhizopus
Know vegetative propagation examples and its advantages
remember: Binary fission: Amoeba (any plane), Leishmania (definite plane); multiple fission: Plasmodium
Hydra: budding and regeneration; Spirogyra: fragmentation; Rhizopus: spores in sporangia
Bryophyllum makes new plants from buds in leaf notches
Banana, orange, rose and jasmine are grown vegetatively because they cannot produce seeds
traps: Don't say Plasmodium uses binary fission; it uses multiple fission
Vegetative propagation gives plants like the parent, not new varieties
Variation comes from imperfect DNA copying, not from the parents choosing it

learn.hook: A hibiscus flower is a complete baby-making kit — and bees are the delivery partners!
points: Sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents, giving more variation. Germ cells carry half the usual DNA, so the zygote gets the full amount.
Flower parts: stamens are male (anther makes pollen grains); the pistil (carpel) is female, with stigma, style and ovary containing ovules, each with an egg cell.
Bisexual flowers have both stamens and pistil (Hibiscus, mustard); unisexual flowers have only one (papaya, watermelon).

Pollination: transfer of pollen from anther to stigma — self-pollination (same flower) or cross-pollination (another flower) by wind, water or animals. A pollen tube grows down the style to the ovule, and the male germ cell fuses with the egg (fertilisation) to form a zygote.

After fertilisation the ovule becomes the seed (with an embryo) and the ovary ripens into the fruit; petals, sepals and stamens may wither and fall. In germination the radicle grows into the root and the plumule into the shoot, using food from the cotyledons.

example.q: Think it through: a papaya tree in a garden never bears fruit, though it flowers every year. What could be the reason?
steps: Papaya flowers are unisexual.
Some papaya plants bear only male flowers.
Without a pistil and ovary, no fruit can develop.
example.answer: It may be a male papaya plant whose flowers have only stamens, so no fruit forms.

learn.reallife: Farmers keep beehives near mustard fields because bees carry pollen from flower to flower, improving cross-pollination.

games.title: From flower to new plant
items: Anther releases pollen
Pollen lands on the stigma (pollination)
Pollen tube grows to the ovule
Male germ cell fuses with the egg (fertilisation)
Ovule becomes seed, ovary becomes fruit
Seed germinates into a seedling

games.title: Match the flower part to what it becomes or does

quiz.q: Which is the female reproductive part of a flower?
quiz.explain: The pistil (carpel) — stigma, style and ovary — is the female part.
steps: Stamens are the male parts (anther makes pollen).
The pistil (carpel) — stigma, style and ovary — is the female part.
Petals and sepals are not reproductive parts.
So the female part is the pistil.
Answer: Pistil

quiz.q: Which of these has unisexual flowers?
quiz.explain: Papaya (and watermelon) flowers have either stamens or pistil, not both.
steps: Unisexual flowers have either stamens or a pistil, not both.
Papaya and watermelon have unisexual flowers.
Hibiscus and mustard have both (bisexual).
So the answer is papaya.
Answer: Papaya

quiz.q: After fertilisation, the ovary develops into the —
quiz.explain: The ovary ripens into the fruit, while ovules become seeds.
steps: After fertilisation, the ovules become seeds.
The ovary ripens into the fruit.
So the ovary develops into the fruit.
Answer: Fruit

quiz.q: What is pollination?
options: Transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma
Fusion of male and female germ cells
Growth of a seed into a plant
quiz.explain: Pollination is only the transfer of pollen; fertilisation happens later in the ovule.
steps: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma.
Fusion of germ cells (fertilisation) happens later in the ovule.
So pollination = transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma.
Answer: Transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma

quiz.q: Which part of the seed grows into the future shoot?
quiz.explain: The plumule becomes the shoot; the radicle becomes the root; cotyledons store food.
steps: A seed has a radicle, a plumule and cotyledons.
The radicle becomes the root; the cotyledons store food.
The plumule grows into the shoot.
So the answer is the plumule.
Answer: Plumule

quiz.q: Why do germ cells carry only half the amount of DNA of other body cells?
options: So that the zygote formed by fusion has the normal amount of DNA
Because they do not need DNA
To make the plant grow faster
quiz.explain: If germ cells had full DNA, it would double every generation. Halving keeps the amount constant.
steps: The zygote is formed by fusion of two germ cells.
If each carried full DNA, the amount would double every generation.
With half each, the zygote gets the normal amount.
So germ cells carry half the DNA so that the zygote has the normal amount.
Answer: So that the zygote formed by fusion has the normal amount of DNA
quiz.mistake: Thinks DNA amount does not matter

quiz.q: Cross-pollination means pollen is transferred —
options: From one flower to the stigma of another flower
From the stigma to the anther
From the seed to the fruit
quiz.explain: In cross-pollination, pollen reaches the stigma of a different flower, often by wind, water or animals.
steps: Self-pollination: pollen reaches the stigma of the same flower.
Cross-pollination: pollen goes from one flower to the stigma of another flower.
Wind, water or animals often carry it.
So cross-pollination is transfer from one flower to the stigma of another.
Answer: From one flower to the stigma of another flower

quiz.q: Where does fertilisation take place in a flowering plant?
options: In the ovule inside the ovary
quiz.explain: The pollen tube carries the male germ cell through the style to the ovule, where it fuses with the egg.
steps: The pollen tube grows down the style to the ovule.
The male germ cell fuses with the egg cell inside the ovule.
So fertilisation takes place in the ovule inside the ovary.
Answer: In the ovule inside the ovary
quiz.mistake: Thinks fertilisation happens on the stigma

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How does a mustard flower become a seed that grows into a new plant?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Pollen reaches the stigma, fertilisation makes a zygote, and the ovule becomes a seed!
teach.nudge: Nice! What must happen after pollination for a seed to form?

revise.summary: In flowering plants, stamens make pollen and the pistil holds ovules. Pollen reaches the stigma (pollination), a pollen tube carries the male germ cell to the egg (fertilisation), and the ovule becomes a seed while the ovary becomes the fruit.
focus: Name the male and female parts of a flower
Tell bisexual from unisexual flowers and self- from cross-pollination
Explain fertilisation, seed and fruit formation, and germination
remember: Stamen (anther) = male; pistil (stigma, style, ovary) = female
Papaya and watermelon have unisexual flowers; Hibiscus and mustard are bisexual
Radicle → root; plumule → shoot; cotyledons store food
traps: Pollination is not fertilisation; it is only the transfer of pollen
The ovary becomes the fruit, not the seed
Germ cells carry half the DNA so the zygote gets the normal amount

learn.hook: Growing up brings many changes — understanding them with science helps us stay healthy and respectful!
points: Puberty is the period when the reproductive organs mature and the body changes, e.g. growth of hair in new areas; in boys the voice deepens, and in girls breasts develop. It happens at different ages for different people.

Male system: testes make sperm and the hormone testosterone. They lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum because sperm formation needs a lower temperature than normal body temperature. Sperm travel through the vas deferens; seminal vesicles and the prostate add fluid.

Female system: the two ovaries make oestrogen, and every month one of them releases an egg. The egg passes into the oviduct (fallopian tube), where fertilisation can occur. The embryo implants in the uterus and gets nutrition and oxygen from the mother through the placenta; development takes about nine months.
If the egg is not fertilised, the thickened, blood-rich lining of the uterus breaks down and comes out as menstruation, roughly every month, lasting about 2 to 8 days.

Reproductive health: some infections spread through sexual contact — bacterial (gonorrhoea, syphilis) and viral (warts, HIV-AIDS). Contraceptive methods include barriers such as condoms (which also reduce infection spread), hormonal pills, devices like the copper-T, and surgical methods (vasectomy, tubectomy). In India, the law bans finding out or revealing a baby's sex before birth, to prevent sex selection.

example.q: Think it through: why are the testes located in the scrotum, outside the abdominal cavity?
steps: Sperm formation needs a temperature lower than normal body temperature.
The scrotum keeps the testes slightly outside the body.
So they stay cooler than the abdomen.
example.answer: Because sperm formation needs a lower temperature than the normal body temperature.

learn.reallife: School health programmes and doctors encourage teenagers to ask questions about body changes openly — accurate information keeps everyone healthy.

games.title: Match the part to its job
pairs: Passes nutrition and oxygen to the embryo

items.q: Barrier method that also reduces infection spread?
Tissue linking embryo to mother's blood?
Surgical method that blocks the vas deferens?

quiz.q: Why are the testes located outside the abdominal cavity?
options: Because sperm formation needs a temperature lower than body temperature
Because there is no space inside
quiz.explain: Sperm are formed best at a slightly lower temperature, which the scrotum provides.
steps: Sperm formation needs a temperature lower than normal body temperature.
The scrotum, outside the abdominal cavity, provides this.
So the testes lie outside the abdomen for sperm formation at a lower temperature.
Answer: Because sperm formation needs a temperature lower than body temperature
quiz.mistake: Thinks warmer is better for sperm

quiz.q: Where does fertilisation normally take place in the human female?
quiz.explain: The egg is fertilised in the oviduct; the embryo then moves to the uterus and implants.
steps: Every month an ovary releases an egg into the oviduct.
Fertilisation normally takes place in the oviduct (fallopian tube).
The embryo then moves to the uterus and implants.
So the answer is the oviduct.
Answer: Oviduct (fallopian tube)
quiz.mistake: Thinks fertilisation happens in the uterus

quiz.q: What is the function of the placenta?
options: To provide nutrition and oxygen to the embryo from the mother's blood and remove its wastes
quiz.explain: The placenta has villi on the embryo's side that exchange glucose, oxygen and wastes with the mother's blood.
steps: The embryo grows inside the uterus.
Through the placenta it gets nutrition and oxygen from the mother's blood.
Wastes from the embryo are removed the same way.
So the placenta provides nutrition and oxygen and removes wastes.
Answer: To provide nutrition and oxygen to the embryo from the mother's blood and remove its wastes
quiz.mistake: Confuses the placenta with the ovary

quiz.q: Menstruation occurs when —
options: The egg is not fertilised and the uterus lining breaks down
quiz.explain: Without fertilisation, the thick uterine lining is not needed, so it breaks down and comes out.
steps: The uterus lining becomes thick and blood-rich each month to receive an embryo.
If the egg is not fertilised, this lining is not needed.
It breaks down and comes out as menstruation.
Answer: The egg is not fertilised and the uterus lining breaks down

quiz.q: Which disease is caused by a virus and can spread through sexual contact?
quiz.explain: HIV-AIDS (and warts) are viral; gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial.
steps: Sexually spread infections can be bacterial or viral.
Gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial.
HIV-AIDS (and warts) are viral; TB is not mainly spread by sexual contact.
So the answer is HIV-AIDS.
Answer: HIV-AIDS
quiz.mistake: Mixes up viral and bacterial infections

quiz.q: Which contraceptive method also helps prevent the spread of sexually transmitted infections?
quiz.explain: A condom is a physical barrier, so it reduces infection spread as well as preventing pregnancy.
steps: A condom is a physical barrier.
It prevents pregnancy and also reduces the spread of infections.
Pills, the copper-T and tubectomy do not stop infections.
So the answer is the condom.
Answer: Condom
quiz.mistake: Thinks every contraceptive protects against infections

quiz.q: In a vasectomy, which part is blocked?
quiz.explain: Vasectomy blocks the vas deferens so sperm cannot be transferred; tubectomy blocks the fallopian tubes.
steps: In a vasectomy the tube that carries sperm in males is blocked.
That tube is the vas deferens.
Tubectomy blocks the fallopian tubes in females.
So the vas deferens is blocked.
Answer: Vas deferens

quiz.q: Which statement about prenatal sex determination in India is correct?
options: It is banned by law, to prevent sex selection
It is required for every pregnancy
It is allowed whenever parents ask for it
quiz.explain: Indian law bans finding out or revealing a baby's sex before birth, to prevent sex selection, protect the girl child and keep a healthy sex ratio.
steps: In India the law bans finding out or revealing a baby's sex before birth.
This prevents sex selection and protects the girl child.
So prenatal sex determination is banned by law, to prevent sex selection.
Answer: It is banned by law, to prevent sex selection
quiz.mistake: Is unaware of the legal ban

teach.ask: Gappu asks shyly: 'Why do teachers say reproductive health is important? How can people stay safe?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Knowing about infections and safe methods like condoms, and asking a doctor, keeps people healthy!
teach.nudge: Good! Can you name one way infections spread, and one way to prevent them?

revise.summary: At puberty the reproductive organs mature. Testes make sperm and testosterone; ovaries make eggs and oestrogen. Fertilisation happens in the oviduct, the embryo grows in the uterus fed through the placenta, and good reproductive health needs knowledge of infections and contraception.
focus: Trace the male and female reproductive systems and their functions
Explain fertilisation, implantation, the placenta and menstruation
Know sexually transmitted infections and contraceptive methods
remember: Testes lie in the scrotum because sperm need a lower temperature than body temperature
Fertilisation occurs in the oviduct (fallopian tube); development takes about nine months
Bacterial: gonorrhoea, syphilis; viral: warts, HIV-AIDS
Vasectomy blocks the vas deferens; tubectomy blocks the fallopian tubes; condoms also reduce infection spread
traps: Fertilisation is not in the uterus; the embryo only implants there
Menstruation happens when the egg is not fertilised
Prenatal sex determination is banned by law in India
